full_judgment:
Md Rezaul Hasan, J: This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 13-7-2017, passed by the Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet, in Family Appeal No.48 of 2016, affirming the judgment and decree dated 21-6-2016 (decree signed on 30-6-2016), passed by the Assistant Judge, Bianibazar & Family Court, Sylhet, in Family Suit No.14 of 2015, decreeing the suit should not be modified and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 4. The Trial Court, after hearing the parties and having assessed the evidence on record, had decreed the suit on 21-6-2016 (decree signed on 30-6-2016). 

 5. Being aggrieved thereby, the defendant has preferred Family Appeal No.48 of 2016, which was heard by the Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet, and the appellate court has dismissed the same and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court in Family Suit No. 14 of 2015. 

 6. Being dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the appellate court, the defendant-appellant has filed this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the instant Rule. 

 7. Learned Advocate M Moshiur Rahman has appeared for the defendant-appellant-petitioner, as noted herein before. He has challenged the calculation of amount payable to the plaintiff-respondent-opposite party. He submits that, at the time of pronouncement of the judgment passed by the trial court on 21-6-2016, the age of infant was 45 months, but the trial court had awarded Taka 2,08,000 as maintenance for 52 (fifty two) months, instead of 45 (forty five) months and thereby, on the date of judgment, the trial court has allowed 7 (seven) months excess maintenance for the infant, at the rate of Taka 4,000 (four thousand) per month, which comes at Taka 28,000. He further submits that, the appellate court as the last court of fact, did not correct this mistake. He concluded submitting that, the finding of the appellate court is liable to be set-aside and the judgment and decree may be modified in accordance with law. He prays that, the Rule has merit and the same may be made absolute. 

 8. Learned Advocates Mr MA Jabber has appeared for the plaintiff-respondent-opposite party. He frankly conceded that, in passing the judgment and decree, the trial court had allowed an excess amount of Taka 28,000 (twenty eight thousand) i.e. for 7 months maintenance of the minor infant (7 x 4,000). The learned Advocate has submitted a supplementary-affidavit on 22-11-2020, in which he has calculated the amount as per the judgment and decree of the trial court and as upheld by the appellate court, however, by adjusting Taka 28,000 (twenty eight thousand) paid in excess as maintenance to the infant, at the time of passing the judgment and decree by the trial court. He has next drawn my attention to the paragraph-9 of the supplementary-affidavit and submits that, after adjustment of the aforesaid 28,000 (twenty eight thousand), a total amount of Taka 6,34,500 becomes payable as decreetal debt. The learned Advocate next drawn my attention to the documentary and oral evidence on record, and further submits that, the plaintiff has proved her case by consistent and adequate oral and documentary evidence. He also submits that, although the defendant had testified as DW 1 and produced another person as DW 2, but the defendant could not establish the defense case with reference to the evidence given by them, while the defendant has failed to produce any appropriate documentary evidence. He further submits that, although the defendant had claimed in his pleading to have sent some amount of money through postal money order, as maintenance of the plaintiff, however, the defendant was not able to produce or to prove any money order or any other documents before the court below in support of his claim about payment of maintenance to the plaintiff or to the infant.. He also submits that, the conduct of the defendant has proved that, he is not a credible person. The learned Advocate next submits that, the trial court has discussed all necessary issues in view of the documentary and oral evidence on record and found that, the plaintiff has been able to prove her case and had decreed the suit. The learned Advocate also submits that, the appellate court, as 'a last court of fact, and has discussed all evidence on record as well as the points for determination, and the appellate court has concurred with the findings of the trial court and has rightly dismissed the appeal. The learned Advocate concludes submitting that, the petitioner has no case and the court below has rightly passed the impugned judgments and decree and that the court below has committed no error of law, nor that has resulted in any error in the decision given, nor the impugned decision has occasioned in failure of justice. Therefore, the Rule has no merit and the same may be discharged with exemplary cost. 

 10. I find that, the marriage between the parties is an admitted fact and it is also admitted that, there was an infant, born out of the wedlock of the parties. I also find that, this suit for dissolution of marriage alongwith claim for dower money and the maintenance of the plaintiff and of the infant has been decreed by the trial court, vide it judgment and decree dated 21-6-2016 (decree signed on 30-6-2016). 

 11. I also find that, the trial court has discussed all evidence on record and has rightly decided all the issues infavour of the plaintiff, having arrived at the correct findings, except a minor calculation mistake as regards the maintenance of the infant, as noted herein before. I also find that, the appellate court had dismissed the appeal on contest and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 12. Having discussed the present revisional application, supplementary-affidavit (filed on 22-11-2020), judgment and decree alongwith the evidence on record, I do not find any misreading or non reading of any evidence and the courts below have arrived at correct findings. 

 13. I also find that, in passing the impugned judgment and decree the appellate court has committed no error of law and that same has not resulted in any error in the decision, nor has occasioned in failure of justice. Rather the defendant had tried to linger this matter, since 2016 till now. 

 19. It should be noted here that, at pragraph-9 of the supplementary-affidavit dated 22-11-2020, the plaintiff has made a calculation of her claim as per judgment and decree of the court below, by adjusting Taka 28,000 (twenty eight thousand) paid in excess. Now, in total Taka 6,34,500 (six lac thirty four thousand and five hundred) is payable. 

 22. In view of the forgoing discussion, I find no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. This Rule has no merit 

 Accordingly, the Rule is discharged with appropriate direction. The impugned judgment and decree dated 13-7-2017, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet, in Family Appeal No.48 of 2016, affirming the judgment and decree dated 21-6-2016 (decree signed on 30-6-2016), passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Bianibazar and Family Court, Sylhet, in Family Suit No.14 of 2015 is hereby up held. 

 The defendant is directed to pay to the plaintiff Taka 6,34,500 (six lac thirty four thousand and five hundred only) within 60 (sixty) working days, at a time or in four equal installments, from the date of receiving copy of this judgment and order alongwith the LCR by the concerned trial court, failing which the petitioner shall remain liable to pay penal interest on the said amount, at the rate of Taka 200 (two hundred) per day, to the plaintiff till realization of the judgment debt, in full, which shall be recovered through the Family Execution Case No. 9 of 2016, pending before the Court of Assistant Judge, Bianibazar, Sylhet, by attaching and selling the assets of the defendant, and/or by attaching the proceeds in his bank account (if any) and directing the bank to pay the said amount (not exceeding the decreetal debt) to the plaintiff, through court, or by directing his employer and/or the creditor to pay the same to the plaintiff (through court), for which, if required, a garnishee order may be passed and/or by detaining him in civil prison and or by seizing his passport (if any) and prohibiting his leaving the country, by passing appropriate order on the immigration authority. 

 Send down the copy of the Judgment and decree alongwith LCR records at once.
